subject: Renewal amendment: reserved GPU top-up and burst guardrail proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@finlytics.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion + burst behavior question

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the renewal ping. Our Q3 usage spiked unexpectedly (attached workbook) and we need to revisit the Dedicated pool we put in place earlier this year. Two asks from my side: 1) can we add ~16 more reserved GPUs on top of our current pool for the next term, and 2) we need clarity on what happens when we exceed reserved capacity — do requests fail, queue, or spill to on-demand? We run production traffic and can't tolerate hard failures.

Procurement wants a quick sketch of pricing and the mechanics so they can start internal approvals. Also looping procurement so they have context.

Thanks,
Sarah Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure | FinLytics
Attachment: FinLytics_usage_q3_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@finlytics.ai>
Cc: FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + burst behavior question

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the data. I reviewed Q3 numbers and we can design an amendment that adds 16 reserved GPUs and a burst orchestration layer that avoids hard failures. High level options: 

- Option A (soft overflow): keep reserved pool + automatic on-demand spill to our hosted fleet. Traffic is routed with priority to reserved capacity; overflow is met immediately with pay-as-you-go pricing and a configurable monthly cap. Avoids queueing or errors but costs more during sustained spikes.

- Option B (hard cap + queue): strictly enforce the reserved pool; excess requests are queued or rejected depending on your retry policy. Lower cost baseline but higher risk of failed requests during spikes.

- Option C (hybrid guardrails): reserved pool + a configurable safety buffer (pre-purchased burst credits) that give a cheaper tail than raw on-demand, with automatic throttles to protect latency SLOs.

I attached a proposed amendment and a pricing matrix for the burst choices. If you prefer, we can draft language that guarantees a baseline throughput (e.g., sustained X tokens/sec across the pool) and an SLO for 95th percentile request latency under reserved capacity.

Next step — would you like a price/term recommendation from our side or should we sketch all three options for Procurement to pick? Happy to join a 30m call this week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_amendment_redwood_v1.pdf (PDF), burst_pricing_matrix.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + burst options — internal pricing suggestion

Olga / team — forwarding Sarah's note. Quick internal take before we reply to FinLytics: 

- Recommend primary: Option C (hybrid). Offer a 12-month amendment with immediate +16 GPUs reserved and a 50k GPU-minute burst credit pool that is cheaper than on-demand.
- Alternative tier: base +24 GPUs with a 10% discount on burst credits if they commit to the larger tier.
- SLO language: commit to baseline throughput and 95th percentile latency < 150ms for traffic served from reserved capacity; reserve language will explicitly exclude hosted overflow.

Can Dev confirm the credit accounting and whether we can program a hard monthly spend cap on on-demand fallback (Aditya)? We should avoid surprises on the invoice.

-Marissa
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + burst options — internal pricing suggestion

On the tech side: Option C is implementable with existing infra and minimal runtime changes. Implementation notes: 

- Provision the reserved pool (+16 GPUs) in their dedicated tenant and enable a soft overflow route to our hosted fleet. The overflow path uses priority routing with token-bucket throttles per customer and a configurable credit counter.
- Burst credits: credit units expressed as GPU-minute equivalents. Credits decrement in real time; once credits are exhausted we fall back to on-demand at a higher rate or start shedding low-priority traffic according to configured policies.
- Spend cap: we can enforce a monthly hard cap on on-demand spend and trigger circuit-breaking; system will notify customer at 80% utilization of the cap.

Note: we can SLO reserved capacity behavior but overflow is best-effort and tied to hosted fleet variability. Legal should redline any broad SLO claims about overflow.

-Dev
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@finlytics.ai>
Cc: FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + burst behavior question

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the usage file and the quick turn on requirements. Based on internal input we've put together a recommendation that balances reliability and cost: 

Recommendation summary:
- Add 16 reserved GPUs to your Dedicated pool for the upcoming 12-month term.
- Adopt the hybrid guardrail (Option C): a 50k GPU-minute burst credit pool + automatic soft overflow to hosted on-demand when credits are exhausted.
- Enforce a monthly on-demand spend cap with an 80% notification threshold (FinLytics to select cap level).
- Amendment will include a baseline throughput paragraph for reserved capacity and an explicit note that overflow performance is best-effort and subject to hosted fleet variability.

Attached is a redline of the amendment and a pricing matrix showing net monthly charges for the options. Proposed timeline: review amendment this week, Procurement issues PO by next Tuesday, we sign and provision within 5 business days of PO.

If that sounds good, can Procurement confirm the internal approval path and desired spend cap? Happy to join a 30m call with technical stakeholders.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_amendment_redwood_v1.pdf (PDF), burst_pricing_matrix.csv (CSV)
